info.title: Marketly API
info.description: Design of the Marketly marketplace API: Customer Store (website + Android app), Seller Center, Admin Center and Operations. One backend, organised in removable modules. Generated from docs/api/spec/*.json.

store.title: Store API
store.audience: Customers and guests on the website and the Android app
store.auth: Every request carries a token: a visitor token (guests, issued when the app opens) or a customer access token.

seller.title: Seller API
seller.audience: Seller owners and seller staff in Seller Center (website + Android app)
seller.auth: Seller member session. Every request acts for one seller account; seller member permissions apply.

admin.title: Admin API
admin.audience: Internal staff in the Admin Center and Operations Center
admin.auth: Staff session. Role permissions and approval limits apply.

public.title: Public API
public.auth: Visitor token of any app. Refresh and sign-out take the refresh token; the bootstrap endpoint takes an app proof.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.auth: Provider signature header, verified per provider

auth.visitor: Any valid token of the app: a visitor token (before sign-in) or a signed-in access token
auth.shopper: A store token that can hold a cart: visitor (guest) or customer
auth.account: Any signed-in account, any realm (self-service security endpoints)
auth.seller: Seller member acting for the seller in the token; optional `permission` narrows it
auth.staff: Staff member (email and password sign-in); optional `permission` narrows it
auth.refresh: Refresh token only (website: the cookie of the app named by audience in the body; Android: refreshToken in the body)
auth.bootstrap: No token: an app proof (Play Integrity or bot challenge). Only POST /api/public/identity/app-sessions

bytes.desc: File size in bytes (media sizeBytes), shown next to attachments and evidence files

fileName.desc: The file's name as uploaded (media fileName), e.g. for attachments and evidence lists

thumbUrl.desc: Product images only: the thumbnail rendition (cards, lists, cart, orders, gallery strip); null for other files

detailUrl.desc: Product images only: the detail rendition (product page); null for other files. url is the size the response asked for (product pages: detail)

state.desc: Tone of the event, so screens can colour the history the same way everywhere (G58c); absent where the owning module does not set one

nextCursor.desc: Cursor for the next batch; null on the last page

key.desc: File name inside the export ZIP without extension, e.g. messages, reviews, store_credit

title.desc: Heading in the export's index, e.g. Messages

records.desc: Plain records about the customer (their own words, choices and amounts). Other people's personal details are left out or masked; internal staff notes are never included.

attachmentIds.desc: Media assets the customer uploaded that belong in the ZIP (message attachments, review photos)

label.desc: e.g. Halden Aurora ANC Wireless Headphones

meta.desc: Short second line, e.g. Product · $149.00, Restaurant · Pizza

path.desc: Store path the website and the app open, e.g. /p/halden-aurora/{id}

available.desc: Shown in the store now (published, active, approved)

cursor.desc: Opaque cursor from the previous response. Used by the Android app's infinite scroll.

page.desc: 1-based page number. Used by the website's numbered pages.

pagination.response: { items: T[], nextCursor: string|null, page?: int, totalPages?: int, total?: int }

VALIDATION_FAILED.meaning: Fields are missing or invalid. details.issues lists each field.

UNAUTHORIZED.meaning: No token, or the token is invalid, expired or revoked (details.reason token_*), or this session can't use the endpoint (details.reason, e.g. sign_in_required, session_idle). Refresh only when details.reason starts with token_.

FORBIDDEN.meaning: Signed in, but the role or seller permission does not allow this. details.permission names it; other refusals give details.reason.

NOT_FOUND.meaning: The record does not exist or is not visible to this caller.

ILLEGAL_TRANSITION.meaning: The status does not allow this action (e.g. approving a rejected product). details.from, details.event.

APPROVAL_REQUIRED.meaning: Above the caller's limit or needs a second reviewer, and nothing was saved (the action cannot be recorded until it is approved). details.approvalRequestId tracks it. When the module saves the record pending approval it answers its normal success status instead, with `approval` (ApprovalInfo) in the body (FORMAT.md, Approval responses).

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.meaning: The Idempotency-Key was used with a different request (path, query or body).

RATE_LIMITED.meaning: Too many requests; retry after the Retry-After header (seconds, also in details.retryAfterSeconds).

NOT_IMPLEMENTED.meaning: Designed but not built yet, or planned for a later launch phase (details.reason not_built or later_phase).

INTERNAL_ERROR.meaning: Something went wrong on the server, or a response did not match the spec. Include the X-Request-Id when reporting it.

RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE.meaning: File downloads (GET /files/…): the requested Range is outside the file. details.sizeBytes.

WRONG_AUDIENCE.meaning: The token is for another app (store, Seller Center or Admin Center).

STEP_UP_REQUIRED.meaning: A fresh proof is needed: a re-auth token for this purpose in the body (reauthToken, from the app's re-auth endpoint). details.kind (reauth), details.purpose.

OWNER_ONLY.meaning: Only the seller owner can do this.

NO_SELLER_ACCESS.meaning: This account cannot act for that seller (or for any seller).

UPGRADE_REQUIRED.meaning: This Android app version is no longer supported; update the app. details.minVersionCode, details.updateUrl.

SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: A service needed to authorize the request is unavailable; retry later.

SERVICE_BUSY.meaning: The rows this request needs were contended and it was retried as far as it can be; send it again. Retry-After says how long to wait. (docs/10-mysql-migration.md D8)

headers.Authorization: Bearer <token> on every request: visitor token before sign-in, access token after (customer, seller member or staff)
headers.Idempotency-Key: Required on endpoints marked idempotent (orders, payments, refunds, payouts). Same key + same request returns the first result (with Idempotent-Replayed: true).
headers.Accept-Language: Ignored: every response is en-US (the only locale at launch)
headers.Accept-Encoding: Optional. gzip, br or zstd: answers of text or JSON over 1 KB come back encoded (Content-Encoding, Vary: Accept-Encoding), and HTTP clients decode them for you. Files served from /files are sent as they are stored
headers.X-Request-Id: Optional. A value of 1–100 letters, digits, _ or - becomes the request id; otherwise the server makes one. Every response carries it; include it when reporting problems
headers.X-App-Proof: Bootstrap only: turnstile:<token> (website bot challenge) or play:<token> (Android Play Integrity); dev in development and tests
headers.X-Client: web, android/<versionCode> or android/<versionName>+<versionCode> (e.g. android/1.4.2+142): analytics and the minimum-version check (426) only, never trusted for authorization
headers.X-Requested-With: Any value. Required with the website's refresh cookie on refresh and sign-out, together with an allowed Origin (else 403)

OFFICIAL_STORE_ID.desc: Seller id of the Official Store, used wherever a seller id is required (feedback, reviews, returns terms, conversations, report facts, promotion lines). The sellers module never issues it.

OFFICIAL_STORE_NAME.desc: Display name of the Official Store wherever a seller name is shown (cart, checkout, orders, conversations, reviews, returns, notices). Use this constant instead of writing the label.

stack.why: Types keep 30+ modules safe to change
Lightweight and fast; one plugin per module fits add/remove
One schema drives validation, types and this documentation

stack.choice: GraphQL (Mercurius), read-only, store / seller / admin schemas
stack.why: One round trip for screens that combine many modules; every write stays on REST
No ORM magic; each module owns a schema; MongoDB swap is per module behind repository interfaces

stack.choice: Job scheduler interface (in-process first, Postgres queue later)
stack.why: Payout runs, deadlines, ad schedules, payment checks
Modules never read each other's tables
Each module boots alone in a test

moduleRules: Each module owns its PostgreSQL schema; no foreign keys across modules, only ids.
Other modules may use only its contract: public API functions, types and events.
Dependencies are declared; the server refuses to start if one is missing and names it.
Disable a module in one config line; delete its folder to remove it; its tables stay until you drop them.
Every list pages two ways: cursors for the Android app, page numbers for the website.
Money is integer cents with a currency; anything that moves money or creates orders is idempotent.
Statuses change only through declared state machines; material staff actions are audited with a reason.
